title: review (other model, opus): D5 fix round 1 on task/T-0194 — delta 38d91fe..28d0fad (T-0194, executed by claude:sonnet)
spec: Review ONLY the T-0194 delta: `git diff 38d91fe 28d0fad` in worktree wt/T-0194 (orchestrator/scorecard.py, orchestrator/cli.py, tests/test_scorecard.py, README.md). Fix round for review T-0191; confirm: (1) planner transcript tokens read from day_tokens per account in the real pool shape (fixture built with pool._save_planner_account) and shown once as a footer under --by goal, never as a per-goal column; (2) per-goal planner column shows decision runs from planner_runs.json with "-" (file missing) / "0 runs" / "n runs" distinguished, plus usd when present; (3) an other bucket collects challenge/triage/unknown roles and total_usd covers every child task (2.0 + 5.0 → 7.0 test); (4) format helper returns str in every path; sys.argv restored via addCleanup; a numeric cell asserted in the --by goal output; (5) default scorecard output still byte-identical (existing test). Also confirm the token formula still matches spawn.run_claude (input + output + cache_read // 10), nothing reads transcript content, malformed jsonl and missing task files are skipped. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_scorecard -q` once. Second review of D5: approve unless a defect would print wrong cost figures in production; smaller points as notes. Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments.
acceptance: Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments
Each of the five T-0191 groups confirmed resolved or named unresolved with evidence
Token formula and default-output guarantee confirmed

comments.issue: Unresolved acceptance item (T-0186 spec point 5, re-asked in this task): malformed jsonl is NOT skipped. `e = json.loads(line)` is unguarded, so one truncated line in runs/*.jsonl aborts the whole command. Reproduced on a scratch root with a half-written line: by_task raises JSONDecodeError, and by_goal raises the same via scorecard.py:220 on a truncated tasks/T-*.json. Note it is consistent with the module's existing readers (build() at scorecard.py:49 and cli.cost at cli.py:19 are equally unguarded), and log_run appends are small single writes, so the exposure is low — hence a note, not a block. A try/except json.JSONDecodeError: continue in both loops closes it.

The doc advertises the goal split as 'percent of usd' with no caveat, but Codex execute runs never log a usd field (executor.py:79 passes tokens only; only spawn.run_claude sets usd=total_cost_usd at spawn.py:156). Live data today is all-Claude so every run carries usd and the table is correct (verified: 125.24 total matches across --by task and --by goal), but the first Codex-executed goal will render execute% ~0 and attribute the goal's whole cost to reviews. executor.py is out of scope here, so this is a caveat to state in the README (or a follow-up task), not a change to make in this diff.

planner_runs.json has no writer anywhere in the repo (D3/T-0122 has not landed; grep over *.py/*.sh/*.md finds only this reader, the README line and the tests). The shape is therefore assumed, not verified: a JSON list of dicts. If T-0122 lands a dict keyed by goal id, `r.get("goal_id")` runs against str keys and `scorecard --by goal` dies with AttributeError. An isinstance(runs, list) guard (returning [] otherwise) would make the reader fail soft the way its FileNotFoundError path already does.

The --by task total row prints tokens as a float because total_tokens is seeded from the shared `= 0.0` at cli.py:141, while every data row prints an int. Live output: rows show `941890`, the total shows `21987302.0`. Seed total_tokens = 0 separately.

_planner_runs_for_goal swallows json.JSONDecodeError into [], but by_goal only branches on runs_path.exists(), so a corrupt planner_runs.json yields planner={'n_runs': 0} and the cell prints '0 runs'. That contradicts format_planner_runs_cell's own docstring claim that '-' means 'we never wrote it' and '0 runs' means 'genuinely none' — the distinction the fix round was asked to add. Propagating the decode failure as the missing case would keep the invariant.

`usd_vals = [r["usd"] for r in runs if "usd" in r]` sums only the records that carry usd, while n_runs counts all of them, so a mixed file renders e.g. '5 runs ($0.40)' where the $0.40 covers 2 of the 5. Either require usd on every record before showing a figure, or mark it partial.
